question: The _________ is a strong, dusty, gusty, hot and dry summer wind from the west which blows over the western Indo-Gangetic Plain region of North India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Loo.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The Loo is a **strong, dusty, gusty, hot, and dry summer wind **from the west which blows over **the western Indo-Gangetic Plain region of North India and Pakistan.**
 
• Loo winds originate over the Iranian, Baloch, and Thar deserts.
 
• It is especially strong in the months of **May and June.**
 
• Due to its very high temperatures (45 °C–50 °C or 115 °F–120 °F), exposure to** it often leads to fatal heatstrokes.**
 
• 
 
Since it causes **extremely low humidity and high temperatures**, the Loo also has a **severe drying effect on vegetation** leading to widespread browning in the areas affected by it during the months of May and June

 Term
 Meaning
 Context/Significance
 
 

 Kaal Baisakhi
 A seasonal storm or unseasonal rainfall, often accompanied by strong winds.
 Primarily occurs in April in parts of North India (especially in Bengal and Assam), marking the start of the Baisakhi festival. It is an unpredictable event and can cause sudden and severe weather disturbances.
 
 

 Sameer
 A common name in India, meaning air or breeze in Sanskrit.
 Used as a name for individuals but also symbolically refers to a gentle breeze in various cultural contexts, especially in poetry and songs.
 
 

 Uttarayan
 Refers to the sun's journey northward in the zodiac, as per Hindu tradition.
 It marks the Makar Sankranti festival, when the sun begins its movement towards the northern hemisphere. Uttarayan is celebrated with kite flying, especially in Gujarat and Rajasthan.
